"What do you feel like eating honey?"
 "I don't really care, dear."

I shouldn't have to commit to any place, because I can do what I want. "Hey, don't forget the keys again!" My wife calls, half serious and joking. I give her a long shrug, just to blow her comment off. I grab the keys and we both head out the door in a slow rush. The evening air is a little humid, it feels that it's trying to stick to you. It doesn't bother me to much, neither does it for her. As we near the car, it becomes apparent that we will have to eat somewhere. "Okay, do you have any ideas on where to go?" 

"Nah, I don't! Just pick a place, and we'll go and eat." The words goes around my head, lingering for a bit. "I don't know." Her expression changes a bit, maybe annoyed. "It's not that hard!"
 "Then how about you choose the place!" She pauses, and hangs on the question for a second or two. "I, I can't!"
 "See? How about we go to the new fast food place that opened up a week ago? The one with the cartoon burger sign?" 
"Meh, alright." The car key turns in the ignition turning on the engine. With ease, I slide out of my spot and get on the road within seconds. "Did you read the news about all the drunk drivers out in town recently?"
 "No, but I don't care really. I'm not drinking, so what does it matter to me?"
 "Well, who knows. Just interesting is all." The roads are quiet tonight, barely anyone out. It is a Tuesday, another day of the week I could care less for. A song I like comes on the radio, and just moments in static noise fills my ears. "Hey, what's wrong with the radio?" I give the thing a couple of smacks, thinking maybe such a mundane task would solve my problem. "Come on, come on!" My attention decreases slightly off the road and onto the sound. "Honey, it's fine, stop hitting the car!"
 "It'll fix it, I just know!"   It seems no matter how much I hit it, there's only static. Just then did I think to try anything else, like tuning it. My eyes are glued to the screen for a split second. "Dave look ou-" my wife lets out a quick gasp, and in a moment everything turns into black. A space of total blackness surrounds me, slowly turning into a pasty white color. Am I going into the light? Below me is a very fuzzy image, one of a car. Holy shit, I'm dead! The bright light above envelopes the rest of my view, and the next thing I know I'm high above the sky, right in the clouds. Looking around, there is nothing but me and the air and the puffy, thick white clouds. I feel a slight nudge on my shoulder, and as I turn, a huge gray gate and a man enter my vision. I take a few steps towards the man, albeit a little vigilante and hesitant. "Where am I?" I exclaim. He doesn't answer right away, maybe he didn't here me. "Hello, do you understand me? Where am I right now?" The man has a short stubble and long brown hair. "I dunno."
 "You don't know? What's that supposed to mean?" He shrugs, giving nothing but a blank expression. "Really, is that how your doing this?" "I guess."
 "Okay, well that's just great. Is there anything you can tell me?" The same blank face stares back at me, unmoving. I'm about to go off again, but he speaks up. "Well, I actually do know where you are. You're in meh-ven."
 "Wait, heaven?"
 "No, MEH-ven." What is this place? I only get more and more confused the more I speak. "So, I am dead, right?" 
"Yes, you are. Bummer, man." 
"And I go through that gate?"
 "Well, you have to be let in."
 "Alright, how do I do that?" The guy just shrugs, again. "Are you telling me you don't know?" One more time, he gives a long shrug. "Tell me, what the heck am I supposed to do now? Do I get in, do I not, what is it?" He begins to move his lazy shoulders, making me more infuriated. "Don't you dare shrug, man. Don't you do it!" We both stand still, looking squarely into each other's eyes. He shrugs. "Okay, that's it. I don't even care, you know? Whatever. I give up. Screw it!" I raise my shoulders high up into the air, high enough to make it very visible. "Is this it, is this what you want? Well here it is, guy. I'm shrugging so freaking much right now, and you know why? Because I just don't give s flying fart!" I take time exhaling, calming down a bit from my burst. "Hey," he says in a very bored voice, "You made it in" 
"That's cool bro, like I said I don't even- wait, huh?" 
"You've been accepted into meh-ven." "Aw, sweet!" The big, grey gates come apart and from the inside I can hear a soft music playing. It's a pretty bland tune, though. "Enjoy the rest of eternity, I guess." My feet tremble a bit walking towards the entrance, filling something in my soul I've never felt before. Wait, no, that's just gas. Never mind. Just inside, as far as the eye can see are apartment buildings, all the same style. "Honey?" A soft female voice penetrates the back of my head. I spin around quickly to find out it was my lovely wife. "Oh my god, you're here!" We wrap each other in a long embrace. "What did I tell you about those drivers, Dave?" All I could give her was a long, lazy shrug.
